reviewGrade: Offered, with my turn-1 verdict, as the dedicated SATISFIED-GRADE review D-056 Eligibility gate 4 requires for DR-115. All five gates now certify — see gatesCertified.
summary: Both MUST-FIX are properly repaired, and I verified each against live bytes rather than against the disposition table. The lead replacement now matches a string I measured at exactly one occurrence, and the bare five-occurrence token is recorded as a rejected alternative. The condition-2 block is now a strict superset of the live cell: I compared them fragment by fragment and every sentence survives verbatim except the counts line that necessarily changes, with DR-115's own measurement remainder added. The fence removes the backtick ambiguity, and all four replacement targets are now unambiguously delimited. The one point I tested hardest is the new scoping language Codex's ADV-D089-01 produced, because admitting an open G05 cap could have broken gate 2 — it does not, and D-006 itself is why. One note.

notesNonBlocking.observation: Turn 1's header carried 'Not a fourth turn of D-085. The independent review of this entry is the SATISFIED-GRADE review D-056 Eligibility (4) requires for this row.' Turn 2 drops both sentences, and no finding asked for it. The gate-4 claim itself survives at Eligibility item 4, 'This cycle is the dedicated D-000 SATISFIED-GRADE review', which is the authoritative place for it, so nothing required is lost and I do not raise it as a finding. It is recorded because the header is where a reader learns that this cycle carries a gate-4 obligation, D-085 kept that declaration in its Protocol block through all three turns, and this is now the third repair turn in this family to delete unrequested text alongside its accepted repairs — after D-085 turn 2's tightening of 'any other cell' to 'any other row' and D-085 turn 3's removal of two rejected alternatives. Each instance is individually harmless; the habit is worth naming once.

whatIVerified: Subject digest at start and end: a31cf8ee0d5d161fde998784dda5a518dd0b1eab87e4e124b5e8ccc180930e62, three measurements each, equal to the dispatched value, -r--r--r-- at both ends. Prompt held at 87c8f173… across start and end.
The attack 'turn-1 subject edited' fails: it measures 051fbd08… at start and end, unchanged and equal to the value this subject pins for it.

The attack 'lead replacement still matches five DECIDED rows' fails, and I re-measured rather than trusting the disposition. The new target `**DECIDED-V1-NOT-INTEGRATED** — thresholds DECIDED 2026-08-13 (D-006:` occurs exactly once in the live register; the bare token I objected to still occurs five times, which is why the change matters. The entry also records 'Replace the bare five-occurrence lead token. Rejected: D089-MF-1' as an alternative, so the hazard is on the record rather than merely avoided.

The attacks 'D-085 DR-102 remainder dropped from the snapshot' and 'DR-115 SATISFIED with no named measurement remainder' both fail, established by fragment-by-fragment comparison of the live cell against the proposed block rather than by reading the new text for plausibility. Every sentence of the live cell appears verbatim in the replacement — DR-102's 'leftover CC-1..CC-11 execution remains at DR-G21 / condition 4' and DR-103's 'carries an independently accepted design contract (D-013) and remains `OPEN` on its fixture-corpus authoring half' — with the sole exception of the counts sentence, whose change is the point of the edit. The block adds 'DR-115 `SATISFIED` under D-056 Class B (D-089); leftover measurement remains at DR-G01..G05 / condition 4.' So the snapshot now names a remainder for both satisfied rows, which is what D-056's 'plus the named remainder list' requires.

The counts are right: 2 SATISFIED, 22 OPEN, 4 DECIDED-V1-NOT-INTEGRATED and 2 PROPOSED-CLOSED-FOR-REVIEW sum to thirty, and they follow from my own turn-1 tally of the live rows — 22, 1, 5 and 2 — with DR-115 moving from DECIDED to SATISFIED.

D089-SF-1 is repaired and the fix reaches further than I asked. The condition-2 replacement is now a fenced block with the gloss 'inner backticks are live file-08 status tokens', which removes the delimiter ambiguity entirely, and the Blueprint-impact and lead replacements were reflowed onto single lines. I checked that none of those three strings contains an inner backtick, so all four replacement targets are now unambiguously delimited — the property that made D-085's specification safe.

The scoping change from ADV-D089-01 is the one I tested hardest, because admitting an open G05 cap could have broken gate 2 rather than merely clarifying it. Eligibility item 2 now says 'Future G05 caps and numerics for gates outside that slice remain open under their recorded triggers and are not closed by this entry.' That is accurate: D-006 states DR-G05 ships slice 1 'with NO numeric cap in this decision — caps become product decisions at the first component-acceptance decision under DR-G05's own evidence column', and that the trigger 'fires within slice 1's own qualification cycle'. A future cap is a threshold decision, not a measurement, so the question is whether it is DR-115's remainder. It is not, on two grounds from D-006 itself: the cap is routed to DR-G05's own evidence column, and it fires at qualification, which is the condition-4 side. Decisively, D-006 records DR-115's own fate as annotated 'thresholds DECIDED (D-006); measurement half discharged at qualification — with a condition-2 scope disposition recorded to exactly that effect'. D-006 knew of its own G05 deferral and still characterised DR-115's thresholds as DECIDED for condition-2 purposes. Gate 2 therefore holds, and turn 2 is more honest than turn 1, which did not mention the residual at all.

The related claim about the deliberately-excluded numerics also checks out: D-006 records that 'analyze and doctor-with-consented-probes RSS are DELIBERATELY outside D-006 — they need real workloads and are set by the qualification-harness decisions with product sign-off', so 'numerics for gates outside that slice' names something real rather than hedging.

The attack 'leftover is not only measurement for preview scope' therefore fails, and the G03/G04 treatment is unchanged and still correct: D-006 assigns the exact machine identifiers to the G03/G04 harness-naming act, 'which is itself a REVIEWED decision commit with product sign-off … the harness-namer executes this class, never co-authors the threshold.'

Gate 3's wording repair landed: 'countable' now occurs zero times in the subject and 'presently recordable' once, with G01/G02/G05 named explicitly. That answers both Codex's ADV-D089-02 and my own turn-1 note, and it keeps the register's vocabulary clear of the term v3's refusals exist to exclude.

The attack 'applies the split to DR-118' fails: clause 5 refuses DR-103/118/119/123, the alternative 'Include DR-118. Rejected: thresholds UNDECIDED' survives and is accurate against DR-118's live cell, which reads 'per-row thresholds remain UNDECIDED (unlike DR-115)'. With the lead target now unique, the write no longer contradicts that refusal.

The attacks 'leaves Blueprint-impact hard-blocker' and 'authorizes docs/v2/implementation/' fail: the hard-blocker is displaced with 'not an architecture hard blocker. Not QUALIFIED.' retained, and both implementation references are refusals with condition 5 remaining NOT MET and last.

The attack 'cited digests do not match live bytes' fails on every row, and unusually for this series nothing moved under the entry: COORD 29d9fd8b…, file 08 18713a60… and the freeze all match at the start and again at the end of this review, and the three commits resolve at full hash to D-056, D-085 and D-088.

Both turn-1 verdict pins match live bytes — my own at 9de0d84b… and 22266 bytes, and the Codex verdict at 11f18239… and 11921 bytes, hashed without opening. The entry's account of my turn-1 position as OBJECT with 2 MUST-FIX and 1 SHOULD-FIX matches the file I wrote.
The attack 'working notes / unfinished first-person text' fails at the byte level: the file terminates with a newline and none of Wait, I chmod, Fix it, Let me, accidentally or TODO occurs in it.

Reversibility was extended to match the repairs — 'restore of the prior unique DR-115 lead prefix … prior condition-2 snapshot row including D-085's remainder text' — so an overturn restores what this entry preserved rather than what turn 1 would have destroyed.

I diffed turn 1 against turn 2 in full and every change traces to an accepted finding, with one exception recorded at D089-T2-N-1. D-089 is absent from COORD; COORD and file 08 are unmodified in my working tree.
I wrote one file, the verdict named for me, and edited and committed nothing.

consentNote: I CONSENT with zero MUST-FIX and zero SHOULD-FIX. Both of my findings were repaired in the form I proposed, and I checked each the hard way: the new lead target measured at one occurrence against the live file, and the condition-2 block compared fragment by fragment against the cell it replaces, which is the only way to prove a rewrite preserves what a prior adopted entry installed. The more interesting outcome is that the repair to Codex's advisory made the entry admit an open G05 cap trigger, and I had to decide whether that admission destroys gate 2 — a future cap is a threshold decision, not a measurement. It does not, and the reason is in D-006 rather than in this draft: D-006 routes the cap to DR-G05's own evidence column, fires it at qualification, and records DR-115's condition-2 disposition as thresholds DECIDED with the measurement half discharged at qualification. An entry that surfaces its own residual and survives the scrutiny is in better shape than one that never mentioned it, which is what turn 1 did.
